guide.summary: Temples, shrine gardens, the deer park and the Heijo Palace Site, with breakfast spots, lunches, dinners, bars and a bakery checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Plan around fixed closures: Isuien Garden and the Harushika Brewery Shop close on Tuesdays, Shika no Fune Kamado and Rokumei Bakes on Wednesdays, and Akordu and Hiraso's Nara shop on Mondays.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: Isuien Garden and the Harushika Brewery Shop close on Tuesdays, Shika no Fune Kamado and Rokumei Bakes on Wednesdays, and Akordu and Hiraso's Nara shop on Mondays. Shika no Fune Saezuri closes on both Tuesdays and Wednesdays.

toolkit.label: Tickets
toolkit.copy: Todai-ji charges adults ¥800 each for the Great Buddha Hall, Hokke-dō, Kaidan-dō and the Todai-ji Museum. Isuien Garden's ¥1,200 general ticket includes the Neiraku Museum, and Yakushi-ji charges adults ¥1,000.

toolkit.label: Walk-in
toolkit.copy: Shika no Fune Kamado takes no reservations and stops serving lunch when the rice runs out, around 15:00, and the Nara Hotel tea lounge does not accept bookings. Rokuen normally needs no reservation, while Azekura requires one for sushi and teppanyaki.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: Nara Prefecture prohibits feeding the deer anything except shika senbei, and Nara Park has no bins, so carry your rubbish out. Deer can butt, bite or kick, so keep children close.

guide.dek: Start at Todai-ji and Kasuga Taisha early, then check each restaurant's closing day before you build the afternoon around it.
intro: Nara's headline sights cluster around Nara Park. At Todai-ji, the Great Buddha Hall opens 7:30–17:30 from April to October and 8:00–17:00 from November to March, while Hokke-dō and the Senju-dō at the Kaidan-in keep 8:30–16:00. Adults pay ¥800 each for the halls and the Todai-ji Museum. Kasuga Taisha's gates open 6:30–17:30, and special worship at the main sanctuary runs 9:00–16:00 for ¥700. The shrine's Manyo Botanical Garden opens 9:00–16:30; it closes on Tuesdays from June to March and opens daily in April and May.

The deer are wild, and the prefecture's rules are clear: feeding them is prohibited except for shika senbei, the park has no bins, and deer can butt, bite or kick, especially mothers in spring and males in autumn. The Nara Deer Preservation Foundation opens its Rokuen enclosure 10:00–16:00 with free entry, a suggested ¥100 contribution and normally no booking. For a quieter hour, Isuien Garden opens 9:30–16:30, closes on Tuesdays, and its ¥1,200 general ticket includes the Neiraku Museum.

West of the centre, Yakushi-ji welcomes you 9:00–17:00, with tickets sold until 16:30 and adult entry at ¥1,000. At the Heijo Palace Site, the Heijo-kyu Izanai-kan visitor hall opens 9:00–17:00 and closes on the second Monday of February, April, July and November, while Suzakumon gate opens 9:00–16:30 and closes on Mondays. Toshodai-ji and Gango-ji have both posted autumn 2026 notices on their own sites, so check those pages for special viewings before you go.

For food, Shika no Fune Kamado in Naramachi serves ¥2,200 lunch sets from 11:00 until the rice runs out, around 15:00, takes no reservations and closes on Wednesdays. Rokumei Coffee's Nara shop opens 8:00–18:00, and Rokumei Bakes sells ¥350 croissants from 8:00 but closes on Wednesdays. Akordu serves lunch and dinner, takes bookings through TableCheck and closes on Mondays. Harushika's brewery shop pours five sakes for ¥700 until 16:30 last order and closes on Tuesdays.
summaryCards: Start at Todai-ji, whose Great Buddha Hall opens at 7:30 from April to October and 8:00 from November to March, then walk on to Kasuga Taisha, open 6:30–17:30.
Have a croissant at Rokumei Bakes from 8:00 on any day but Wednesday, then visit Isuien Garden from 9:30 on any day but Tuesday.
Akordu takes reservations through TableCheck and closes on Mondays, as does Hiraso's Nara shop, while Shika no Fune Kamado takes no reservations at all.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability, and temples and shrines note that hours can change for ceremonies. Kofuku-ji and Horyu-ji (certificate errors), the Nara National Museum (HTTP 403), the Nara Prefectural Museum of Art (expired certificate), Kamameshi Shizuka (DNS failure) and the Irie Taikichi photography museum (no readable content) could not be read, so they are left out; a failed fetch is not evidence of closure. Hours were not published on the pages read for Toshodai-ji, Gango-ji, Nara Hotel Mikasa and Nara Hotel The Bar, and closing days were not stated for Rokumei Coffee's Nara shop or the Kasuga Taisha Treasure Hall. JW Marriott Hotel Nara hours come from an undated dining page, and individual venue pages had been removed. Isuien Garden's guide page has no dated notices. The Nara Deer Preservation Foundation's site lists two unrelated blog entries about link building, which may indicate spam on that site. Shin-Yakushiji, Naramachi Koshi-no-ie and several food shops published addresses but no 2026 content.
